name: Field of Giants
summary: The Field of Giants spreads across the southern Barrens, from Camp Taurajo to Dustwallow's marshes. Towering kodo, thunder lizards, and other great beasts graze its dry scrub, while silithids make the plain more dangerous.

sections.title: A Wild Frontier in the South
sections.body: The Field of Giants follows the southern Gold Road, far from the Barrens' better-defended north. Wooden watchtowers along the road sit largely abandoned, while great herds roam the open flats. Hunters and naturalists come to see Kalimdor's enormous beasts, but the land is not safe. Dwarven excavators from Bael Modan dig aggressively to the south, and a more sinister threat has begun burrowing underground.

sections.title: The Creeping Swarm
sections.body: Silithid hives have recently broken through the ground across the Field of Giants. They mark the northernmost known sighting of these ravenous creatures in Kalimdor. Their strange mounds and aggressive swarms have alarmed the Horde. Korran, a troll scout from the Crossroads, and Ruga Ragetotem, a tauren warrior at Camp Taurajo, urge adventurers to investigate the hives and learn what draws these horrors so far from the deep deserts.

faq.q: Why is it called the Field of Giants?
faq.answer: The plain takes its name from its enormous wildlife. Great herds of towering kodo and thunder lizards graze here, alongside other massive Kalimdorean beasts.

faq.q: What are those bug mounds in the ground?
faq.answer: Those mounds belong to silithids, insectoid predators that have tunneled up from deep underground. Their hives are the northernmost discovered in Kalimdor, and they threaten travelers and local wildlife.

faq.q: Who lives near the Field of Giants?
faq.answer: Few settlements lie on the plain itself, but the tauren shaman Brine lives on a southern ridge. Nearby, the displaced exile Gann Stonespire watches and plots against the dwarven excavation at Bael Modan.

faq.q: Why are the watchtowers along the road abandoned?
faq.answer: The Horde concentrates its forces along the northern Gold Road near the Crossroads, so the southern reaches receive fewer patrols. The towers have been neglected amid silithid threats and aggressive wildlife.

angles.text: Thunder lizards and massive kodo roam the Field of Giants, making it one of the Barrens' premier hunting grounds for hunters seeking formidable beasts.
Silithid hives near the road between Camp Taurajo and Dustwallow Marsh threaten travel through the Barrens. Leaders across the region are calling for scouts.
